_comment: High-confidence secret patterns for hooks/core/security-scan.sh. Every entry must be a
vendor-prefixed token, a PEM header, or a credential-bearing URL -- something that is almost
certainly a real secret when it appears. ADR 0005 deleted the heuristic `credentials` group
(password\s*[:=]\s*...) because it fired on `password: str`, `secret: string`, and
`API_KEY=os.environ[...]`; a scanner that cries wolf gets switched off, and a switched-off
scanner has zero recall. Precision over recall -- do not add value-less keyword patterns here.
ERE syntax as understood by BOTH BSD (macOS) and GNU grep -E: no \s, no \d, no lookaround.
Matching is case-SENSITIVE; the vendor prefixes carry their own casing.
`placeholder_suppression` is matched against the MATCHED TOKEN (not the line): a hit whose
every match looks like documentation boilerplate is not reported. It is what keeps AWS's own
AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE and postgres://user:password@localhost out of the results.
